$.description: The $ object provides a number of debugging facilities and informational methods.

properties.name: build
properties.description: The ExtendScript build information.

properties.name: buildDate
properties.description: The ExtendScript build date.

properties.name: decimalPoint
properties.description: The character used as the decimal point character in formatted numeric output.

properties.name: engineName
properties.description: The name of the current ExtendScript engine, if set.

properties.name: error
properties.description: The most recent run-time error information. Assigning error text to this property generates a run-time error; however, the preferred way to generate a run-time error is to throw an Error object.

properties.name: fileName
properties.description: The file name of the current script.

properties.name: flags
properties.description: Gets or sets low-level debug output flags. A logical AND of bit flag values: 0x0002 (2): Displays each line with its line number as it is executed. 0x0040 (64): Enables excessive garbage collection. Usually, garbage collection starts when the number of objects has increased by a certain amount since the last garbage collection. This flag causes ExtendScript to garbage collect after almost every statement. This impairs performance severely, but is useful when you suspect that an object gets released too soon. 0x0080 (128): Displays all calls with their arguments and the return value. 0x0100 (256): Enables extended error handling (see strict). 0x0200 (512): Enables the localization feature of the toString method. Equivalent to the localize property.

properties.name: global
properties.description: A reference to the global object, which contains the JavaScript global namespace.

properties.name: hiresTimer
properties.description: A high-resolution timer, measuring the time in microseconds. The timer starts when ExtendScript is initialized during the application startup sequence. Every read access resets the timer to Zero.

properties.name: includePath
properties.description: The path for include files for the current script.

properties.name: level
properties.description: The current debugging level, which enables or disables the JavaScript debugger. One of 0 (no debugging), 1 (break on runtime errors), or 2 (full debug mode).

properties.name: line
properties.description: The current line number of the currently executing script.

properties.name: locale
properties.description: Gets or sets the current locale. The string contains five characters in the form LL_RR, where LL is an ISO 639 language specifier, and RR is an ISO 3166 region specifier.Initially, this is the value that the application or the platform returns for the current user. You can set it to temporarily change the locale for testing. To return to the application or platform setting, set to undefined, null, or the empty string.

properties.name: localize
properties.description: Set to true to enable the extended localization features of the built-in toString() method.

properties.name: memCache
properties.description: The ExtendScript memory cache size, in bytes.

properties.name: os
properties.description: The current operating system version information.

properties.name: screens
properties.description: An array of objects containing information about the display screens attached to your computer. Each object has the properties left, top, right, bottom, which contain the four corners of each screen in global coordinates.A property primary is true if that object describes the primary display.

properties.name: stack
properties.description: The current stack trace.

properties.name: strict
properties.description: Sets or clears strict mode for object modification. When true, any attempt to write to a read-only property causes a runtime error. Some objects do not permit the creation of new properties when true.

properties.name: version
properties.description: The version number of the ExtendScript engine. Formatted as a three-part number and description; for example: "3.92.95 (debug)".

methods.description: Create a mini-folio out of asset and overlay descriptions. Schema for the mini folio description: || Key || Type || Required? || Description || | contentstackid | string | yes | The explicit ID to be used for this stack | | tocImage | file | no | The TOC image for the mini-folio | | narrowdimension | int | no | Targetted export size, measured along narrow dimension | | widedimension | int | no | Targetted export size, measured along wide dimension | | smoothscrolling | @enum(SmoothScrollingOptions) | no | The smooth scrolling behavior for this stack (default is noSmoothScroll) | | locationforgeneratedassets | file | no | If included, this is an existing directory where the generated assets should be created. | | overlays | array | no | see the SDK Overlay Builder APIs | | assets | array | yes | The assets for the mini - folio, described below. | | assetDependencies | array | no | Files that are needed by the asset, that will be included in the package but not the manifest. | | metadata | array | no | The metadata for the mini-folio described below. | | showprogressbar | boolean | no | Either true or false to indicate whether we should show a progress bar (default is false) | | targetviewerversion | string | no | If provided (in the form "major.minor.revision") a folio compatible with the viewer version is produced. If omitted, the latest folio format is produced. | CS5 | The following are fields in the array for "assets": || Key || Type || Required? || Description || | file | file | yes | The asset file | | type | string | yes | The asset file type, either "web" for HTML or "image" for a raster | | width | int | yes | The asset width | | height | int | yes | The asset height | | orientation | string | yes | The asset orientation, either "portrait" or "landscape" | | thumbnail | file | no | A thumbnail of the asset to be used in browse mode | | scrubber | file | no | A thumbnail of the asset to be used in scrubber mode | The following are fields in the array for "assetDependencies": || Key || Type || Required? || Description || | file | file | no | The dependent file | | relativePath | string | no | The relative path to the file, for use in the package | The following are fields in the array for "metadata": || Key || Type || Required? || Description || | any string | string or boolean | no | any key/value where the key is a string, and the value is either a string or a boolean, such as those described in "export folio meta data" |

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: characters
properties.description: A number of characters for which to reserve space when calculating the preferred size of the element.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help string that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: justify
properties.description: The text justification style. One of left, center, or right. Justification only works if this value is set on creation of the element.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). A Button object has no creation properties, but the third argument to the add() method that creates it can be the initial text value.

properties.name: shortcutKey
properties.description: The key sequence that invokes the onShortcutKey() callback for this element (in Windows only).

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: text
properties.description: The text to display, a localizable string.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type; "button".

properties.name: visible
properties.description: True if this element is shown, false if it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

properties.name: window
properties.description: The window that this element belongs to.

properties.name: windowBounds
properties.description: The bounds of this element relative to the top-level parent window.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.description: Registers an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this element.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event. Event names are listed in the JavaScript Tools Guide.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: The function that handles the event. This can be the name of a function defined in the extension, or a locally defined handler function to be executed when the event occurs. A handler function takes one argument, the UIEvent object.

parameters.name: capturePhase
parameters.description: When true, the handler is called only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. Default is false, meaning that the handler is called in the bubbling phase if this object is an ancestor of the target, or in the at-target phase if this object is itself the target. (default: false)

methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the element's shortcutKey sequence is typed in the active window.

Checkbox (SUI).name: Checkbox (SUI)
Checkbox (SUI).description: A dual-state control showing a box that has a checkmark when the value is true, and is empty when the value is false.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: characters
properties.description: A number of characters for which to reserve space when calculating the preferred size of the element.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: justify
properties.description: The default text justification style for child text elements. One of left, center, or right. Justification only works if this value is set on creation of the element.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the item (properties used only when the element is created). A CheckBox object has no creation properties. The third argument to the add() method that creates it is the text to be displayed.

properties.name: shortcutKey
properties.description: The key sequence that invokes the onShortcutKey() callback for this element (in Windows only).

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: text
properties.description: The text to display, a localizable string.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type; "checkbox".

properties.name: value

methods.name: adjustLayout
methods.description: Adjust the existing layout according to new page size, bleed and margin values. The first parameter is a plain object with key value pairs for properties affected. Permissible keys are width, height, bleedInside, bleedTop, bleedOutside, bleedBottom, leftMargin, topMargin, rightMargin, bottomMargin. The values can be specified as decimal numbers in units of Pt or as a string having a measurement value such as '1 in'. Not all properties need to be specified, only the values that need updation. Notice that when dealing with individual pages rather than the whole document, bleed changes has no effect. E.g. - app.activeDocument.adjustLayout({width:'600px', leftMargin: '1in'}), app.activeDocument.adjustLayout({rightMargin:'1in'}, app.activeDocument.spreads[0].pages), app.activeDocument.spreads[0].pages[0].adjustLayout({width:'400px', leftMargin: '10px'})

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.description: The width and height in pixels of each item in the list. Used by auto-layout to determine the preferredSize of the list, if not otherwise specified. If not set explicitly, the size of each item is set to match the largest height and width among all items in the list

properties.description: The array of choice items displayed in the drop-down or pop-up list. Access this array with a 0-based index. To obtain the number of items in the list, use items.length.The objects are created when items are specified on creation of the parent list object, or afterward using the list control’s add() method. Items in a drop-down list can be of type separator, in which case they cannot be selected, and are shown as a horizontal line. Each item has a selected property that is true when it is in the selected state.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). Creation properties of a DropDownList object can include: items: An array of strings for the text of each list item. An item object is created for each item. An item with the text string "-" creates a separator item. Supply this property, or the items argument to the add() method, not both. When true, the control does not display input text (used for password input fields). enterKeySignalsOnChange: When false (the default), the control signals an onChange event when the editable text is changed and the control loses the keyboard focus (that is, the user tabs to another control, clicks outside the control, or types Enter). When true, the control only signals an onChange() event when the editable text is changed and the user types Enter; other changes to the keyboard focus do not signal the event. wantReturn: Only applies to multiple line edit controls in ScriptUI Version 6.0 or later. When true the RETURN/ENTER keystroke is considered as text-input advancing the cursor to the next line. The default value is false.

File.name: File
File.description: Represents a file in the local file system in a platform-independent manner.

properties.name: absoluteURI
properties.description: The full path name for the referenced file in URI notation.

properties.name: alias
properties.description: If true, the object refers to a file system alias or shortcut.

properties.name: created
properties.description: The creation date of the referenced file, or null if the object does not refer to a file on disk.

properties.name: creator
properties.description: In Mac OS, the file creator as a four-character string. In Windows or UNIX, value is "????".

properties.name: displayName
properties.description: The localized name of the referenced file, without the path specification.

properties.name: encoding
properties.description: Gets or sets the encoding for subsequent read/write operations. One of the encoding constants listed in the JavaScript Tools Guide. If the value is not recognized, uses the system default encoding.A special encoder, BINARY, is used to read binary files. It stores each byte of the file as one Unicode character regardless of any encoding. When writing, the lower byte of each Unicode character is treated as a single byte to write.

properties.name: eof
properties.description: When true, a read attempt caused the current position to be at the end of the file, or the file is not open.

properties.name: error
properties.description: A string containing a message describing the most recent file system error. Typically set by the file system, but a script can set it. Setting this value clears any error message and resets the error bit for opened files. Contains the empty string if there is no error.

properties.name: exists
properties.description: If true, this object refers to a file or file-system alias that actually exists in the file system.

properties.name: fsName
properties.description: The platform-specific full path name for the referenced file.

properties.name: fullName
properties.description: The full path name for the referenced file in URI notation.

properties.name: hidden
properties.description: When true, the file is not shown in the platform-specific file browser. If the object references a file-system alias or shortcut, the flag is altered on the alias, not on the original file.

properties.name: length
properties.description: The size of the file in bytes. Can be set only for a file that is not open, in which case it truncates or pads the file with 0-bytes to the new length.

properties.name: lineFeed
properties.description: How line feed characters are written in the file system. One of the values "Windows", "Macintosh", or "Unix".

properties.name: modified
properties.description: The date of the referenced file's last modification, or null if the object does not refer to a file on the disk.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The file name portion of the absolute URI for the referenced file, without the path specification.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The Folder object for the folder that contains this file.

properties.name: path
properties.description: The path portion of the absolute URI for the referenced file, without the file name.

properties.name: readonly
properties.description: When true, prevents the file from being altered or deleted. If the referenced file is a file-system alias or shortcut, the flag is altered on the alias, not on the original file.

properties.name: relativeURI
properties.description: The path name for the object in URI notation, relative to the current folder.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The file type as a four-character string. In Mac OS, the Mac OS file type. In Windows, "appl" for .EXE files, "shlb" for .DLL files and "TEXT" for any other file.

methods.name: File
methods.description: Creates and returns a new File object referring to a given file system location.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The full or partial path name of the file, in platform-specific or URI format. The value stored in the object is the absolute path. The file that the path refers to does not need to exist.If the path refers to an existing folder: The File function returns a Folder object instead of a File object. The new operator returns a File object for a nonexisting file with the same name.

methods.name: changePath
methods.description: Changes the path specification of the referenced file.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A string containing the new path, absolute or relative to the current folder.

methods.name: close
methods.description: Closes this open file.

methods.name: copy
methods.description: Copies this object’s referenced file to the specified target location.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: A string with the URI path to the target location, or a File object that references the target location.

methods.name: createAlias
methods.description: Makes this file a file-system alias or shortcut to the specified file.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A string containing the path of the target file.

methods.name: decode
methods.description: Decodes a UTF-8 encoded string as required by RFC 2396, and returns the decoded string.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: The UTF-8 encoded string to decode.

methods.name: encode
methods.description: Encodes a string as required by RFC 2396, and returns the encoded string.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The string to encode.

methods.name: execute
methods.description: Executes or opens this file using the appropriate application, as if it had been double-clicked in a file browser.

methods.name: getRelativeURI
methods.description: Retrieves and returns the path for this file, relative to the specified base path, in URI notation.

parameters.name: basePath
parameters.description: A base path in URI notation.

methods.name: isEncodingAvailable
methods.description: Reports whether a given encoding is available.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The encoding name. Typical values are "ASCII", "binary", or "UTF-8". For a complete list of supported encodings, see the JavaScript Tools Guide.

methods.name: open
methods.description: Opens the referenced file for subsequent read/write operations. The method resolves any aliases to find the file.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: The read-write mode, a single-character string. One of these characters: r (read) Opens for reading. If the file does not exist or cannot be found, the call fails. w (write) Opens a file for writing. If the file exists, its contents are destroyed. If the file does not exist, creates a new, empty file. e (edit) Opens an existing file for reading and writing. a (append) Opens an existing file for reading and writing, and moves the current position to the end of the file.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: In Mac OS, the type of a newly created file, a 4-character string. Ignored in Windows and UNIX.

parameters.name: creator
parameters.description: In Mac OS, the creator of a newly created file, a 4-character string. Ignored in Windows and UNIX.

methods.name: openDialog
methods.description: Opens a dialog so the user can select one or more files to open.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: The prompt text, displayed if the dialog allows a prompt.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: A filter that limits the types of files displayed in the dialog. In Windows, a filter expression such as "Javascript files:*.jsx;All files:*.*". In Mac OS, a filter function that takes a File instance and returns true if the file should be included in the display, false if it should not. (default: null)

parameters.name: multiSelect
parameters.description: When true, the user can select multiple files and the return value is an array. (default: false)

methods.name: openDlg
methods.description: Opens the built-in platform-specific file-browsing dialog, in which the user can select an existing file or files, and creates new File objects to represent the selected files.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: A string containing the prompt text, if the dialog allows a prompt.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: A filter that limits the types of files displayed in the dialog. In Windows, a filter expression such as "Javascript files:*.jsx;All files:*.*". In Mac OS, a filter function that takes a File instance and returns true if the file should be included in the display, false if it should not. (default: null)

parameters.name: multiSelect
parameters.description: When true, the user can select multiple files and the return value is an array. (default: false)

methods.name: read
methods.description: Reads the contents of the file, starting at the current position.

parameters.name: chars
parameters.description: An integer specifying the number of characters to read.

methods.name: readch
methods.description: Reads a single text character from the file at the current position.

methods.name: readln
methods.description: Reads a single line of text from the file at the current position.

methods.name: remove
methods.description: Deletes the file associated with this object from disk immediately, without moving it to the system trash.

methods.name: rename
methods.description: Renames the associated file.

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: The new file name, with no path information.

methods.name: resolve
methods.description: Attempts to resolve the file-system alias or shortcut that this object refers to.

methods.name: saveDialog
methods.description: Opens a dialog so the user can select a file name to save to.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: The prompt text, displayed if the dialog allows a prompt.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: In Windows only, a filter that limits the types of files displayed in the dialog. In Windows only, a filter expression such as "Javascript files:*.jsx;All files:*.*". Not used In Mac OS. (default: null)

methods.name: saveDlg
methods.description: Opens the built-in platform-specific file-browsing dialog, in which the user can select an existing file location to which to save information, and creates a new File object to represent the selected file.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: A string containing the prompt text, if the dialog allows a prompt.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: In Windows only, a filter that limits the types of files displayed in the dialog. In Windows only, a filter expression such as "Javascript files:*.jsx;All files:*.*". Not used In Mac OS. (default: null)

methods.name: seek
methods.description: Seeks to a given position in the file.

parameters.name: pos

FlashPlayer (SUI).name: FlashPlayer (SUI)
FlashPlayer (SUI).description: A control that contains a Flash Player, which can load and play Flash movies stored in SWF files.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). A FlashPlayer object has no creation properties.

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type, "flashplayer".

properties.name: visible
properties.description: True if this element is shown, false if it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

properties.name: window
properties.description: The window that this element belongs to.

properties.name: windowBounds
properties.description: The bounds of this element relative to the top-level parent window.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.description: Registers an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this element.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event. Event names are listed in the JavaScript Tools Guide.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: The function that handles the event. This can be the name of a function defined in the extension, or a locally defined handler function to be executed when the event occurs. A handler function takes one argument, the UIEvent object.

parameters.name: capturePhase
parameters.description: When true, the handler is called only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. Default is false, meaning that the handler is called in the bubbling phase if this object is an ancestor of the target, or in the at-target phase if this object is itself the target. (default: false)

methods.name: callback
methods.description: A function definition for a callback from the Flash ActionScript environment.

methods.name: dispatchEvent
methods.description: Simulates the occurrence of an event in this target.

methods.name: hide
methods.description: Hides this element.

methods.name: invokePlayerFunction
methods.description: Invokes an ActionScript function defined in the Flash application.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of a Flash ActionScript function that has been registered with the ExternalInterface object by the currently loaded SWF file.

parameters.name: argument
parameters.description: An argument to pass through to the function. There can be any number of arguments. An argument must be one of these data types:Number, String, Boolean, null, undefined, Object, Array. No other data types are supported.

methods.name: loadMovie
methods.description: Loads a movie into the Flash Player, and begins playing it.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The File object for the SWF file to load.

methods.name: notify
methods.description: Sends a notification message, simulating the specified user interaction event.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the control event handler to call. One of: onClick, onChange, onChanging. By default, simulates the onChange event for an edittext control, an onClick event for controls that support that event.

methods.name: playMovie
methods.description: Restarts a movie that has been stopped.

parameters.name: rewind
parameters.description: When true, restarts the movie from the beginning; otherwise, starts playing from the point where it was stopped. (default: false)

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.description: Unregisters an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this element.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event.

methods.name: stopMovie
methods.description: Halts playback of the current movie.

methods.name: Folder
methods.description: Creates and returns a new Folder object referring to a given file-system location.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The absolute or relative path to the folder associated with this object, specified in URI format. The value stored in the object is the absolute path.The path need not refer to an existing folder. If the path refers to an existing file, rather than a folder: The Folder() function returns a File object instead of a Folder object. The new operator returns a Folder object for a nonexisting folder with the same name.

methods.description: Retrieves the contents of this folder, filtered by the supplied mask.

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: A search mask for file names, specified as a string or a function. A mask string can contain question mark (?) and asterisk (*) wild cards. Default is "*", which matches all file names. Can also be the name of a function that takes a File or Folder object as its argument. It is called for each file or folder found in the search; if it returns true, the object is added to the return array. NOTE: In Windows, all aliases end with the extension .lnk. ExtendScript strips this from the file name when found, in order to preserve compatibility with other operating systems. You can search for all aliases by supplying the search mask "*.lnk", but note that such code is not portable.

FootnoteOption.name: FootnoteOption
FootnoteOption.description: Options for specifying default footnote formatting.

properties.name: continuingRuleColor
properties.description: The swatch (color, gradient, tint, or mixed ink) applied to the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule on is true. Can return: Swatch or String.

properties.name: continuingRuleGapColor
properties.description: The swatch (color, gradient, tint, or mixed ink) applied to the stroke gap of the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule type is not solid. Can return: Swatch or String.

properties.name: continuingRuleGapOverprint
properties.description: If true, overprints the gap color of the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule type is not solid.

properties.name: continuingRuleGapTint
properties.description: The tint (as a percentage) of the gap color of the rule above continued footnote text. (Range: 0 to 100) Note: Valid when continuing rule type is not solid.

properties.name: continuingRuleLeftIndent
properties.description: The amount to left indent the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule on is true.

properties.name: continuingRuleLineWeight
properties.description: The stroke weight of the rule above continued footnote text. (Range: 0 to 1000) Note: Valid when continuing rule on is true.

properties.name: continuingRuleOffset
properties.description: The vertical offset of the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule on is true.

properties.name: continuingRuleOn
properties.description: If true, draws a rule above footnote text that continues from a previous column. Note: Valid when no splitting is false or undefined.

properties.name: continuingRuleOverprint
properties.description: If true, overprints the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule on is true.

properties.name: continuingRuleTint
properties.description: The tint (as a percentage) of the rule above continued footnote text. (Range: 0 to 100) Note: Valid when continuing rule type is not solid.

properties.name: continuingRuleType
properties.description: The stroke type of the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule on is true. Can return: StrokeStyle or String.

properties.name: continuingRuleWidth
properties.description: The length of the rule above continued footnote text. Note: Valid when continuing rule on is true.

properties.name: enableStraddling
properties.description: If true, document will have straddling footnotes. If false, document will not have straddling footnotes.

properties.name: eosPlacement
properties.description: If true, footnotes at the end of the story are placed just below the text. If false, footnotes at the end of the story are placed at the bottom of the column.

properties.name: eventListeners
properties.description: A collection of event listeners.

properties.name: events
properties.description: A collection of events.

properties.name: footnoteFirstBaselineOffset
properties.type: FootnoteFirstBaseline FootnoteFirstBaseline.ASCENT_OFFSET FootnoteFirstBaseline.CAP_HEIGHT FootnoteFirstBaseline.EMBOX_HEIGHT FootnoteFirstBaseline.FIXED_HEIGHT FootnoteFirstBaseline.LEADING_OFFSET FootnoteFirstBaseline.X_HEIGHT
properties.description: The distance between the top of the footnote container and the footnote text.

properties.name: footnoteMarkerStyle
properties.description: The character style to apply to footnote reference numbers in the main text.

properties.name: footnoteMinimumFirstBaselineOffset
properties.description: The minimum distance between the baseline of the text and the top of the footnote container.

properties.name: footnoteNumberingStyle
properties.type: FootnoteNumberingStyle FootnoteNumberingStyle.ARABIC FootnoteNumberingStyle.ARABIC_ABJAD FootnoteNumberingStyle.ARABIC_ALIF_BA_TAH FootnoteNumberingStyle.ASTERISKS FootnoteNumberingStyle.DOUBLE_LEADING_ZEROS FootnoteNumberingStyle.FULL_WIDTH_ARABIC FootnoteNumberingStyle.HEBREW_BIBLICAL FootnoteNumberingStyle.HEBREW_NON_STANDARD FootnoteNumberingStyle.KANJI FootnoteNumberingStyle.LOWER_LETTERS FootnoteNumberingStyle.LOWER_ROMAN FootnoteNumberingStyle.SINGLE_LEADING_ZEROS FootnoteNumberingStyle.SYMBOLS FootnoteNumberingStyle.UPPER_LETTERS FootnoteNumberingStyle.UPPER_ROMAN String
properties.description: The footnote numbering style. Can return: FootnoteNumberingStyle enumerator or String.

properties.name: footnoteTextStyle
properties.description: The paragraph style to apply to footnotes. Note: The space before and after the paragraph defined in the paragraph style is ignored for footnotes. To define space above and between footnotes, see spacer and space between.

properties.name: isValid
properties.description: Returns true if the object specifier resolves to valid objects.

properties.name: markerPositioning
properties.description: The position of footnote reference numbers in the main text. Can return: FootnoteMarkerPositioning enumerator or String.

properties.name: noSplitting
properties.description: If true, footnotes cannot split across columns. If false, footnotes flow into succeeding columns when the footnote text causes the footnote area to expand upward to reach the footnote reference number in the main text.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent of the FootnoteOption (a Application or Document).

properties.name: prefix
properties.description: The prefix text of the footnote. (Limit: 0 to 100 characters)

properties.name: properties
properties.description: A property that allows setting of several properties at the same time.

properties.name: restartNumbering
properties.type: FootnoteRestarting FootnoteRestarting.DONT_RESTART FootnoteRestarting.PAGE_RESTART FootnoteRestarting.SECTION_RESTART FootnoteRestarting.SPREAD_RESTART String
properties.description: The point at which to restart footnote numbering. Can return: FootnoteRestarting enumerator or String.

properties.name: ruleColor
properties.description: The swatch (color, gradient, tint, or mixed ink) applied to the stroke of the rule above the first footnote in the column. Note: Valid when rule on is true. Can return: Swatch or String.

properties.name: ruleGapColor
properties.description: The swatch (color, gradient, tint, or mixed ink) applied to the stroke gap of the rule above the first footnote in the column. Note: Valid when rule type is not solid. Can return: Swatch or String.

properties.name: ruleGapOverprint
properties.description: If true, overprints the gap color of the rule above the first footnote in the column. Note: Valid when rule type is not solid.

properties.name: ruleGapTint
properties.description: The tint (as a percentage) of the gap color of the rule above the first footnote in the column. (Range: 0 to 100) Note: Valid when rule type is not solid.

properties.name: ruleLeftIndent
properties.description: The amount to left indent the rule above the first footnote in the column. Note: Valid when rule on is true.

properties.name: ruleLineWeight
properties.description: The stroke weight of the rule above the first footnote in the column. (Range: 0 to 1000) Note: Valid when rule on is true.

properties.name: ruleOffset
properties.description: The vertical offset of the rule above the first footnote in the column. Note: Valid when rule on is true.

properties.name: ruleOn
properties.description: If true, draws a rule between the text and the first footnote in the column.

properties.name: ruleOverprint
properties.description: If true, overprints the rule above the first footnote in the column. Note: Valid when rule on is true.

properties.name: ruleTint
properties.description: The tint (as a percentage) of the rule above the first footnote in the column. (Range: 0 to 100) Note: Valid when rule on is true.

properties.name: ruleType
properties.description: The stroke type of the rule above the first footnote in a column. Note: Valid when rule on is true. Can return: StrokeStyle or String.

properties.name: ruleWidth
properties.description: The length of the rule above the first footnote in the column. Note: Valid when rule on is true.

properties.name: separatorText
properties.description: The text to insert between the footnote marker number and the footnote text. (Range: 0 to 100 characters)

properties.name: showPrefixSuffix
properties.description: The position of the footnote prefix and/or suffix. Can return: FootnotePrefixSuffix enumerator or String.

properties.name: spaceBetween
properties.description: The amount of vertical space between footnotes. Note: The space before and space after defined for the paragraph style applied to the footnote is ignored.

properties.name: spacer
properties.description: The minimum amount of vertical space between the bottom of the text column and the first footnote. Note: The space before amount defined in the paragraph style applied to the footnote is ignored for the first footnote.

properties.name: startAt
properties.description: The number at which to start footnote numbering.

properties.name: suffix
properties.description: The suffix text of the footnote. (Limit: 0 to 100 characters)

Group (SUI).name: Group (SUI)
Group (SUI).description: A container for other controls within a window.

properties.name: alignChildren
properties.description: Tells the layout manager how unlike-sized children of this container should be aligned within a column or row. Order of creation determines which children are at the top of a column or the left of a row; the earlier a child is created, the closer it is to the top or left of its column or row. If defined, alignment for a child element overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. See alignment property for values.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: layout
properties.description: The layout manager for this container. The first time a container object is made visible, ScriptUI invokes this layout manager by calling its layout() function. Default is an instance of the LayoutManager class that is automatically created when the container element is created.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: margins
properties.description: The number of pixels between the edges of a container and the outermost child elements. You can specify different margins for each edge of the container. The default value is based on the type of container, and is chosen to match the standard Adobe UI guidelines.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: orientation

The allowed values for the container’s alignChildren and its children’s alignment properties depend on the orientation.

IconButton (SUI).description: A mouse-sensitive pushbutton that displays an image instead of text.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: image
properties.description: The image object that defines the image to be drawn.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: location

ListBox (SUI).name: ListBox (SUI)
ListBox (SUI).description: Displays a list of choices, represented by ListItem objects.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child ListItem elements.

properties.name: columns
properties.description: For a multi-column list box, the column properties. A JavaScript object with two read-only properties whose values are set by the creation parameters: titles: An array of column title strings, whose length matches the number of columns specified at creation. preferredWidths: An array of column widths, whose length matches the number of columns specified at creation. visible: An array of boolean visible attributes, whose length matches the number of columns specified at creation.This property can be used to show/hide a column. Avaiblable in ScriptUI Version 6.0 or later provided ScriptUI.frameworkName == 'Flex'.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: itemSize
properties.description: The width and height in pixels of each item in the list. Used by auto-layout to determine the preferredSize of the list, if not otherwise specified. If not set explicitly, the size of each item is set to match the largest height and width among all items in the list

properties.name: items
properties.description: The array of choice items displayed in the list. Access this array with a 0-based index. To obtain the number of items in the list, use items.length.The objects are created when items are specified on creation of the parent list object, or afterward using the list control’s add() method. Each item has a selected property that is true when it is in the selected state.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the control (properties used only when the element is created). Creation properties of a ListBox object can include: multiselect: When false (the default), only one item can be selected. When true, multiple items can be selected. items: An array of strings for the text of each list item. An item object is created for each item. An item with the text string "-" creates a separator item. Supply this property, or the items argument to the add() method, not both. This form is most useful for elements defined using Resource Specifications. numberOfColumns: A number of columns in which to display the items; default is 1. properties.name: selection
properties.description: The currently selected item for a single-selection list, or an array of items for current selection in a multi-selection list. Setting this value causes the selected item to be highlighted and to be scrolled into view if necessary. If no items are selected, the value is null. Set to null to deselect all items. You can set the value using the index of an item or an array of indices, rather than object references. If set to an index value that is out of range, the operation is ignored. When set with index values, the property still returns object references. If you set the value to an array for a single-selection list, only the first item in the array is selected. Panel (SUI).name: Panel (SUI)
Panel (SUI).description: A container for other types of controls, with an optional frame.

properties.name: alignChildren
properties.description: Specifies how to align the child elements.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: characters
properties.description: Reserve space for the specified number of characters; affects calculation of preferredSize .

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: justify
properties.description: The default text justification style for child text elements. One of left, center, or right. Justification only works if this value is set on creation of the element.

properties.name: layout
properties.description: The layout manager for this container. The first time a container object is made visible, ScriptUI invokes this layout manager by calling its layout() function. Default is an instance of the LayoutManager class that is automatically created when the container element is created.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element's frame relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: margins
properties.description: The number of pixels between the edges of a container and the outermost child elements. You can specify different margins for each edge of the container. The default value is based on the type of container, and is chosen to match the standard Adobe UI guidelines.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: orientation
properties.description: The layout orientation of children in a container. Interpreted by the layout manager for the container. The default LayoutManager Object accepts the (case-insensitive) values row, column, or stack. For window and panel, the default is column, and for group the default is row. The allowed values for the container’s alignChildren and its children’s alignment properties depend on the orientation.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the control (properties used only when the element is created). Creation properties of a Panel object can include: borderStyle: A string that specifies the appearance of the border drawn around the panel. One of black, etched, gray, raised, sunken. Default is etched. su1PanelCoordinates: Photoshop only. When true, this panel automatically adjusts the positions of its children for compatability with Photoshop CS. Default is false, meaning that the panel does not adjust the positions of its children, even if the parent window has automatic adjustment enabled.

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: spacing
properties.description: The number of pixels separating one child element from its adjacent sibling element. Because each container holds only a single row or column of children, only a single spacing value is needed for a container. The default value is based on the type of container, and is chosen to match standard Adobe UI guidelines.

properties.name: text
properties.description: The title or label text, a localizable string.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type; "panel".

properties.name: visible
properties.description: True if this element is shown, false if it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

properties.name: window
properties.description: The window that this element belongs to.

properties.name: windowBounds
properties.description: The bounds of this element relative to the top-level parent window.

methods.name: add

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: maxvalue
properties.description: The maximum value in the range. Default is 100.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.description: The minimum value in the range; always 0. If set to a different value, it is ignored.

properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). A ProgressBar object has no creation properties. The third argument of the add() method that creates it is the initial value (default 0), and the fourth argument is the maximum value of the range (default 100).

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.description: True if this element is shown, false if it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

RadioButton (SUI).name: RadioButton (SUI)
RadioButton (SUI).description: A dual-state control, grouped with other radiobuttons, of which only one can be in the selected state.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: characters
properties.description: A number of characters for which to reserve space when calculating the preferred size of the element.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent

methods.name: newBrush
methods.signature: ScriptUIBrush (SUI) newBrush (type:Number, color:Array of Number String)
methods.description: Creates a new painting brush object.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The brush type, solid or theme. One of the constants ScriptUIGraphics.BrushType.SOLID_COLOR or ScriptUIGraphics.BrushType.THEME_COLOR.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The brush color. If type is SOLID_COLOR, the color expressed as an array of three or four values, in the form [R, B, G, A] specifying the red, green, and blue values of the color and, optionally, the opacity (alpha channel). All values are numbers in the range [0.0..1.0]. An opacity of 0 is fully transparent, and an opacity of 1 is fully opaque. If the type is THEME_COLOR, the name string of the theme. Theme colors are defined by the host application.

methods.name: newPath
methods.description: Creates a new, empty path object.

methods.name: newPen
methods.signature: ScriptUIPen (SUI) newPen (type:Number, color:Array of Number String, width:Number)
methods.description: Creates a new drawing pen object.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The pen type, solid or theme. One of the constants ScriptUIGraphics.PenType.SOLID_COLOR or ScriptUIGraphics.PenType.THEME_COLOR.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The pen color. If type is SOLID_COLOR, the color expressed as an array of three or four values, in the form [R, B, G, A] specifying the red, green, and blue values of the color and, optionally, the opacity (alpha channel). All values are numbers in the range [0.0..1.0]. An opacity of 0 is fully transparent, and an opacity of 1 is fully opaque. If the type is THEME_COLOR, the name string of the theme. Theme colors are defined by the host application.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The width of the pen line in pixels. The line is centered around the current point. For example, if the value is 2, drawing a line from (0, 10) to (5, 10) paints the two rows of pixels directly above and below y-position 10.

methods.name: rectPath

parameters.description: The width in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The height in pixels.

parameters.name: pen

parameters.description: The path object. Default is the currentPath.

ScriptUI (SUI).name: ScriptUI (SUI)
ScriptUI (SUI).description: A global class containing central information about ScriptUI. Not instantiable.

properties.name: Alignment
properties.description: Collects the enumerated values that can be used in the alignment and alignChildren properties of controls and containers. Predefined alignment values are: TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT, FILL, CENTER

properties.name: FontStyle
properties.description: Collects the enumerated values that can be used as the style argument to the ScriptUI.newFont() method. Predefined styles are REGULAR, BOLD, ITALIC, BOLDITALIC.

properties.name: applicationFonts

properties.name: compatibility
properties.description: An object whose properties are the names of compatability modes supported by the host application. The presence of ScriptUI.compatability.su1PanelCoordinates means that the application allows backward compatibility with the coordinate system of Panel elements in ScriptUI version 1.

properties.name: coreVersion
properties.description: A string containing the internal version number of the ScriptUI module.

properties.name: environment
properties.description: An object whose properties define attributes of the environment in which ScriptUI operates.

properties.name: events
properties.description: An object whose properties and methods provide access to objects used in the ScriptUI event system. It contains one function, createEvent(), which allows you to create event objects in order to simulate user-interaction event

properties.name: frameworkName
properties.description: A string containing the name of the UI component framework with which this version of ScriptUI is compatible.

properties.name: version
properties.description: A string containing the version number of the ScriptUI component framework
