Scrollbar (SUI).name: Scrollbar (SUI)
Scrollbar (SUI).description: A scrollbar with a draggable scroll indicator and stepper buttons to move the indicator.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: jumpdelta
properties.description: The amount to increment or decrement a scrollbar indicator's position when the user clicks ahead or behind the moveable element. Default is 20% of the range between the maxvalue and minvalue property values.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: maxvalue
properties.description: The maximum value allowed in the value property. Together with minvalue, sets the scrolling range. Default is 100.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minvalue
properties.description: The minimum value allowed in the value property. Together with maxvalue, sets the scrolling range.Default is 0.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). A Scrollbar object has no creation properties. The third argument of the add() method that creates it is the initial value, and the fourth and fifth arguments are the minimum and maximum values of the range.

properties.name: shortcutKey
properties.description: The key sequence that invokes the onShortcutKey() callback for this element (in Windows only).

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: stepdelta
properties.description: The amount by which to increment or decrement a scrollbar element's position when the user clicks a stepper button.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type, "scrollbar".

properties.name: value
properties.description: The current position of the indicator. If set to a value outside the range specified by minvalue and maxvalue, it is automatically reset to the closest boundary.

properties.name: visible
properties.description: True if this element is shown, false if it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

properties.name: window
properties.description: The window that this element belongs to.

properties.name: windowBounds
properties.description: The bounds of this element relative to the top-level parent window.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.description: Registers an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this element.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event. Event names are listed in the JavaScript Tools Guide.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: The function that handles the event. This can be the name of a function defined in the extension, or a locally defined handler function to be executed when the event occurs. A handler function takes one argument, the UIEvent object.

parameters.name: capturePhase
parameters.description: When true, the handler is called only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. Default is false, meaning that the handler is called in the bubbling phase if this object is an ancestor of the target, or in the at-target phase if this object is itself the target. (default: false)

methods.name: dispatchEvent
methods.description: Simulates the occurrence of an event in this target.

methods.name: hide
methods.description: Hides this element.

methods.name: notify
methods.description: Sends a notification message, simulating the specified user interaction event.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the control event handler to call. One of: onClick, onChange, onChanging. By default, simulates the onChange event for an edittext control, an onClick event for controls that support that event.

methods.name: onActivate
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the element acquires the keyboard focus.

methods.name: onChange
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the user has finished dragging the position indicator, or has clicked the control.

methods.name: onChanging
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the content of the element is in the process of changing

methods.name: onDeactivate
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the element loses the keyboard focus.

methods.name: onDraw
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the window is about to be drawn.

methods.name: onShortcutKey
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the element's shortcutKey sequence is typed in the active window.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.description: Unregisters an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this element.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event.

parameters.description: The function that handles the event.

parameters.name: capturePhase
parameters.description: Whether to call the handler only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. (default: false)

Slider (SUI).name: Slider (SUI)
Slider (SUI).description: A slider bar that indicates a numeric value with a moveable position indicator.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: maxvalue
properties.description: The maximum value allowed in the value property. Together with minvalue, sets the range.Default is 100.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minvalue
properties.description: The minimum value allowed in the value property. Together with maxvalue, sets the range.Default is 0.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). A Slider object has no creation properties. The third argument of the add() method that creates it is the initial value, and the fourth and fifth arguments are the minimum and maximum values of the range.

properties.name: shortcutKey
properties.description: The key sequence that invokes the onShortcutKey() callback for this element (in Windows only).

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type, "slider".

properties.name: value
properties.description: The current position of the indicator. If set to a value outside the range specified by minvalue and maxvalue, it is automatically reset to the closest boundary.

properties.name: visible
properties.description: True if this element is shown, false if it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

properties.name: window
properties.description: The window that this element belongs to.

properties.name: windowBounds
properties.description: The bounds of this element relative to the top-level parent window.

methods.description: Registers an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this element.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event. Event names are listed in the JavaScript Tools Guide.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: The function that handles the event. This can be the name of a function defined in the extension, or a locally defined handler function to be executed when the event occurs. A handler function takes one argument, the UIEvent object.

parameters.description: When true, the handler is called only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. Socket.name: Socket
Socket.description: Creates a TCP/IP connection, or establishes a TCP/IP server.

properties.name: connected
properties.description: When true, the connection is active.

properties.name: encoding
properties.description: Sets or retrieves the name of the encoding used to transmit data. Typical values are "ASCII", "BINARY", or "UTF-8".

properties.name: eof
properties.description: When true, the receive buffer is empty.

properties.name: error
properties.description: A message describing the most recent error. Setting this value clears any error message.

properties.name: host
properties.description: The name of the remote computer when a connection is established. If the connection is shut down or does not exist, the property contains the empty string.

properties.name: timeout
properties.description: The timeout in seconds to be applied to read or write operations.

methods.name: Socket
methods.description: Creates a new Socket object.

methods.name: close
methods.description: Terminates the open connection.

methods.name: listen
methods.description: Instructs the object to start listening for an incoming connection.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The TCP/IP port number to listen on. Valid port numbers are 1 to 65535. Typical values are 80 for a Web server, 23 for a Telnet server and so on.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: The encoding to be used for the connection Typical values are "ASCII", "BINARY", or "UTF-8". (default: ASCII)

methods.name: open
methods.description: Opens the connection for subsequent read/write operations.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The server to connect to. This can be a DNS name, an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 address, followed by a colon and a port number.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: The encoding to be used for the connection Typical values are "ASCII", "binary", or "UTF-8". (default: ASCII)

methods.name: poll
methods.description: Checks a listening object for a new incoming connection.

methods.name: read
methods.description: Reads up to the specified number of characters from the connection. CR characters are ignored unless the encoding is set to "BINARY".

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of characters to read. If not supplied, the connection attempts to read as many characters it can get and returns immediately.

methods.name: readln
methods.description: Reads one line of text up to the next line feed.

methods.name: write
methods.description: Concatenates all arguments into a single string and writes that string to the connection.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Any number of string values. All arguments are concatenated to form the string to be written. CRLF sequences are converted to LFs unless the encoding is set to "BINARY".

methods.name: writeln
methods.description: Concatenates all arguments into a single string, appends a LF character, and writes that string to the connection.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Any number of string values. All arguments are concatenated to form the string to be written. CRLF sequences are converted to LFs unless the encoding is set to "BINARY".

properties.name: active
properties.description: Always false. This element cannot have input focus. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: justify
properties.description: The text justification style. One of left, center, or right. Justification only works if this value is set on creation of the element.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). Creation properties of a StaticText object can include: multiline: When false (the default), the control displays a single line of text. When true, the control displays multiple lines, in which case the text wraps within the width of the control. scrolling: When false (the default), the displayed text cannot be scrolled. When true, the displayed text can be vertically scrolled using the Up Arrow and Down Arrow; this case implies multiline=true.

properties.name: shortcutKey

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . TreeView (SUI).name: TreeView (SUI)
TreeView (SUI).description: A hierarchical list whose items can contain child items.

properties.name: active
properties.description: True if this element is active. An active control is the one with keyboard focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, is selected when the user types Return or Enter in Windows, or the space bar in Mac OS.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for this element. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The boundaries of the element, in parent-relative coordinates. Setting an element's size or location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: children
properties.description: An array of child elements.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the element's appearance, in response to the onDraw() event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element during automatic layout. Applies for column orientation and left alignment, or row orientation and top alignment.

properties.name: itemSize
properties.description: The width and height in pixels of each item in the list. Used by auto-layout to determine the preferredSize of the list, if not otherwise specified. If not set explicitly, the size of each item is set to match the largest height and width among all items in the list

properties.name: items
properties.description: The array of top-level items displayed in the list. Access this array with a 0-based index. To obtain the number of items in the list, use items.length.The objects are created when items are specified on creation of the parent list object, or afterward using the list control’s add() method.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of this element relative to its parent. The location is defined as [bounds.x, bounds.y]. Setting an element's location changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The maximum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The minimum height and width to which the element can be resized.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size, used by layout managers to determine the best size for each element. If not explicitly set by a script, value is established by the UI framework in which ScriptUI is employed, and is based on such attributes of the element as its text, font, font size, icon size, and other UI framework-specific attributes.A script can explicitly set this value before the layout manager is invoked in order to establish an element size other than the default.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the control (properties used only when the element is created). Creation properties of a ListBox object can include: items: An array of strings for the text of each top-level list item. An item object is created for each item. An item with the text string "-" creates a separator item. Supply this property, or the items argument to the add() method, not both. This form is most useful for elements defined using Resource Specifications.

properties.name: selection
properties.description: The currently selected list item. Setting this value causes the selected item to be highlighted and to be scrolled into view if necessary. If no items are selected, the value is null. Set to null to deselect all items.You can set the value using the index of an item, rather than an object reference. If set to an index value that is out of range, the operation is ignored. When set with an index value, the property still returns an object reference.

properties.name: shortcutKey
properties.description: The key sequence that invokes the onShortcutKey() callback for this element (in Windows only).

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current dimensions of this element. Initially undefined, and unless explicitly set by a script, it is defined by a LayoutManager . A script can explicitly set size before the layout manager is invoked to establish an element size other than the preferredSize or the default size, but this is not recommended. Defined as [bounds.width, bounds.height]. Setting an element's size changes its bounds property, and vice-versa.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type, "treeview".

properties.name: visible
properties.description: True if this element is shown, false if it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

properties.name: window
properties.description: The window that this element belongs to.

properties.name: windowBounds
properties.description: The bounds of this element relative to the top-level parent window.

parameters.name: capturePhase
parameters.description: When true, the handler is called only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. Default is false, meaning that the handler is called in the bubbling phase if this object is an ancestor of the target, or in the at-target phase if this object is itself the target. (default: false)

Window (SUI).name: Window (SUI)
Window (SUI).description: The instance represents a top-level window or dialog box, which contains user-interface elements.

properties.name: active
properties.description: Set to true to make this window active. A modal dialog that is visible is by definition the active dialog. An active palette is the front-most window. An active control is the one with focus—that is, the one that accepts keystrokes, or in the case of a Button, be selected when the user types Return or Enter.

properties.name: alignChildren
properties.description: Tells the layout manager how unlike-sized children of this container should be aligned within a column or row. Order of creation determines which children are at the top of a column or the left of a row; the earlier a child is created, the closer it is to the top or left of its column or row. If defined, alignment for a child element overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. See alignment property for values.

properties.name: alignment
properties.description: The alignment style for child elements of a container. If defined, this value overrides the alignChildren setting for the parent container. This can be a single string, which indicates the alignment for the orientation specified in the parent container, or an array of two strings, indicating both the horizontal and vertical alignment (in that order). Allowed values depend on the orientation value of the parent container. They are not case sensitive. For orientation=row:top, bottom, fill For orientation=column: left, right, fill For orientation=stack:top, bottom, left, right, fill

properties.name: bounds
properties.description: The bounds of the window's drawable area, excluding the frame, in screen coordinates.

properties.name: cancelElement
properties.description: For windows of type dialog, the UI element to notify when the user presses a cancellation key combination. The cancellation key is the Esc key. By default, looks for a button whose name or text is "cancel" (case disregarded).

properties.name: characters
properties.description: A number of characters for which to reserve space when calculating the preferred size of the window.

properties.name: children
properties.description: The collection of UI elements that have been added to this container. An array indexed by number or by a string containing an element's name. The length property of this array is the number of child elements for container elements, and is zero for controls.

properties.name: defaultElement
properties.description: For windows of type dialog, the UI element to notify when the user presses a Enter key. By default, looks for a button whose name or text is "ok" (case disregarded).

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: True if this element is enabled. An enabled element can accept input, according to its type. When false, control elements do not accept input, and all types of elements have a dimmed appearance.

properties.name: frameBounds
properties.description: The bounds of the window frame in screen coordinates. The frame consists of the title bar and borders that enclose the content region of a window, depending on the windowing system.

properties.name: frameLocation
properties.description: The top left corner of the window frame in screen coordinates. The same as [frameBounds.x, frameBounds.y]. Set this value to move the window frame to the specified location on the screen. The frameBounds value changes accordingly.

properties.name: frameSize
properties.description: The size and location of the window's frame in screen coordinates.

properties.name: graphics
properties.description: The graphics object that can be used to customize the window’s appearance, in response to the onDraw event.

properties.name: helpTip
properties.description: The help text that is displayed when the mouse hovers over the element.

properties.name: indent
properties.description: The number of pixels to indent the element.

properties.name: justify
properties.description: The default text justification style for child text elements. One of left, center, or right. Justification only works if this value is set on creation of the element.

properties.name: layout
properties.description: The layout manager for this container. The first time a container object is made visible, ScriptUI invokes this layout manager by calling its layout() function. Default is an instance of the LayoutManager class that is automatically created when the container element is created.

properties.name: location
properties.description: The upper left corner of the window's drawable area. The same as [bounds.x, bounds.y].

properties.name: margins
properties.description: The number of pixels between the edges of a container and the outermost child elements. You can specify different margins for each edge of the container. The default value is based on the type of container, and is chosen to match the standard Adobe UI guidelines.

properties.name: maximized
properties.description: True if the window is expanded.

properties.name: maximumSize
properties.description: The largest rectangle to which the window can be resized.

properties.name: minimized
properties.description: True if the window is minimized or iconified.

properties.name: minimumSize
properties.description: The smallest rectangle to which the window can be resized.

properties.name: opacity
properties.description: The opacity of the window, in the range [0..1]. A value of 1.0 (the default) makes the window completely opaque, a value of 0 makes it completely transparent. Intermediate values make it partially transparent to any degree.

properties.name: orientation
properties.description: The layout orientation of children in a container. Interpreted by the layout manager for the container. The default LayoutManager Object accepts the (case-insensitive) values row, column, or stack. For window and panel, the default is column, and for group the default is row. The allowed values for the container’s alignChildren and its children’s alignment properties depend on the orientation.

properties.name: parent
properties.description: The immediate parent element.

properties.name: preferredSize
properties.description: The preferred size of the window. Used in automatic layout and resizing. To set a specific value for only one dimension, specify the other dimension as -1.

properties.name: properties
properties.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the container (properties used only when the element is created). Creation properties of a Window object can include: resizeable: When true, the window can be resized by the user. Default is false. su1PanelCoordinates: Photoshop only. When true, the child panels of this window automatically adjust the positions of their children for compatability with Photoshop CS (in which the vertical coordinate was measured from outside the frame). Default is false. Individual panels can override the parent window’s setting. closeButton: Bridge only. When true, the title bar includes a button to close the window, if the platform and window type allow it. When false, it does not. Default is true. Not used for dialogs. maximizeButton: Bridge only. When true, the title bar includes a button to expand the window to its maximum size (typically, the entire screen), if the platform and window type allow it. When false, it does not. Default is false for type palette, true for type window. Not used for dialogs.

properties.name: shortcutKey
properties.description: The keypress combination that invokes this element's onShortcutKey() callback.

properties.name: size
properties.description: The current size and location of the content area of the window in screen coordinates.

properties.name: spacing
properties.description: The number of pixels separating one child element from its adjacent sibling element. Because each container holds only a single row or column of children, only a single spacing value is needed for a container. The default value is based on the type of container, and is chosen to match standard Adobe UI guidelines.

properties.name: text
properties.description: The title, label, or displayed text, a localizeable string. Does not apply to containers of type group.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The element type; "dialog", "palette", or "window".

properties.name: visible
properties.description: When true, the element is shown, when false it is hidden. When a container is hidden, its children are also hidden, but they retain their own visibility values, and are shown or hidden accordingly when the parent is next shown.

properties.name: window
properties.description: The window that this element belongs to.

properties.name: windowBounds
properties.description: The bounds of this window relative to the top-level parent window.

methods.name: Window
methods.description: Creates a new window.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The window type. One of: window: Creates a simple window that can be used as a main window for an application. (Not supported by Photoshop CS3.) palette: Creates a modeless dialog, also called a floating palette. (Not supported by Photoshop CS3.) dialog: Creates a modal dialog. This argument can also be a ScriptUI resource specification; in that case, all other arguments are ignored.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The window title, a localizable string.

parameters.name: bounds
parameters.description: The window's position and size.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: An object containing creation-only properties. Can contain any of these properties: resizeable: When true, the window can be resized by the user. Default is false. su1PanelCoordinates: Photoshop only. When true, the child panels of this window automatically adjust the positions of their children for compatability with Photoshop CS (in which the vertical coordinate was measured from outside the frame). Default is false. Individual panels can override the parent window’s setting. closeButton: When true, the title bar includes a button to close the window, if the platform and window type allow it. When false, it does not. Default is true. Not used for dialogs. maximizeButton: When true, the title bar includes a button to expand the window to its maximum size (typically, the entire screen), if the platform and window type allow it. When false, it does not. Default is false for type palette, true for type window. Not used for dialogs. minimizeButton: When true, the title bar includes a button to minimize or iconify the window, if the platform and window type allow it. When false, it does not. Default is false for type palette, true for type window. Main windows cannot have a minimize button in Mac OS. Not used for dialogs. independent: When true, a window of type window is independent of other application windows, and can be hidden behind them in Windows. In Mac OS, has no effect. Default is false. borderless: When true, the window has no title bar or borders. Properties that control those features are ignored.

methods.name: add
methods.description: Creates and returns a new control or container object and adds it to the children of this window.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of the child element, as specified for the type property. Control types are listed in the JavaScript Tools Guide.

parameters.name: bounds
parameters.description: A bounds specification that describes the size and position of the new control or container, relative to its parent. If supplied, this value creates a new Bounds object which is assigned to the new object’s bounds property.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text or label, a localizable string. Initial text to be displayed in the control as the title, label, or contents, depending on the control type. If supplied, this value is assigned to the new object’s text property.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: An object that contains one or more creation properties of the new child (properties used only when the element is created). The creation properties depend on the element type. See properties property of each control type.

methods.name: addEventListener
methods.description: Registers an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this window.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event. Predefined event names are: change, changing, move, moving, resize, resizing, show , enterKey, focus, blur, keydown, keyup, mousedown, mouseup, mousemove, mouseover, mouseout, click (detail = 1 for single, 2 for double).

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: The function that handles the event. This can be the name of a function defined in the extension, or a locally defined handler function to be executed when the event occurs. A handler function takes one argument, the UIEvent object.

parameters.name: capturePhase
parameters.description: When true, the handler is called only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. Default is false, meaning that the handler is called in the bubbling phase if this object is an ancestor of the target, or in the at-target phase if this object is itself the target. (default: false)

methods.name: alert
methods.description: Displays a platform-standard dialog containing a short message and an OK button.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: TThe string for the displayed message.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: A string to appear as the title of the dialog, if the platform supports a title. Ignored in Mac OS, which does not support titles for alert dialogs. The default title string is "Script Alert".

parameters.name: errorIcon
parameters.description: When true, the platform-standard alert icon is replaced by the platform-standard error icon in the dialog. Ignored in Mac OS, which does not support icons for alert dialogs. (default: false)

methods.name: center
methods.description: Centers this window on screen or with repect to another window.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: The relative window. If not specified, centers on the screen.

methods.name: close
methods.description: Closes this window.

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: A number to be returned from the show() method that invoked this window as a modal dialog.

methods.name: confirm
methods.description: Displays a platform-standard dialog containing a short message and two buttons labeled Yes and No.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The string for the displayed message.

parameters.name: noAsDefault
parameters.description: When true, the No button is the default choice, selected when the user types Enter. Default is false, meaning that Yes is the default choice. (default: false)

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: A string to appear as the title of the dialog, if the platform supports a title. Ignored in Mac OS, which does not support titles for alert dialogs. The default title string is "Script Alert".

methods.name: dispatchEvent
methods.description: Simulates the occurrence of an event in this target.

methods.name: find
methods.description: Use this method to find an existing window.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The name of a predefined resource available to JavaScript in the current application; or the window type. If a title is specified, the type is used if more than one window with that title is found. Can be null or the empty string.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The window title.

methods.name: hide
methods.description: Hides this windows.

methods.name: notify
methods.description: Sends a notification message to all listeners, simulating the specified user interaction event.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The event name; if omitted, the default event is sent. One of: onClose, onMove, onMoving, onResize, onResizing, onShow

methods.name: onActivate
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the window acquires the keyboard focus.

methods.name: onClose
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the window is about to be closed.

methods.name: onDeactivate
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the window loses the keyboard focus.

methods.name: onMove
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the window has been moved

methods.name: onMoving
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called when the window is being moved

methods.name: onResize
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called after the window has been resized

methods.name: onResizing
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called while a window is being resized

methods.name: onShortcutKey
methods.description: In Windows only, an event-handler callback function, called a shortcut-key sequence is typed that matches the shortcutKey value for this window.

methods.name: onShow
methods.description: An event-handler callback function, called just before the window is displayed

methods.name: prompt
methods.description: Displays a modal dialog that returns the user’s text input.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: The string for the displayed message.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: The initial value to be displayed in the text edit field.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: A string to appear as the title of the dialog. In Windows, this appears in the window’s frame; in Mac OS it appears above the message. The default title string is "Script Prompt".

methods.name: remove
methods.description: Removes the specified child control from this window’s children array.

parameters.name: what
parameters.description: The child control to remove, specified by 0-based index, text property value, or as a control object.

methods.name: removeEventListener
methods.description: Unregisters an event handler for a particular type of event occuring in this window.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: The function that handles the event.

parameters.name: capturePhase
parameters.description: Whether to call the handler only in the capturing phase of the event propagation. (default: false)

methods.name: show
methods.description: Makes this window visible.

ArrowHead.name: ArrowHead
ArrowHead.description: The shape of one or both ends of an open path.

values.name: ArrowHead.BARBED_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A solid arrow head whose pierced end bows sharply toward the point and whose point describes a 45-degree angle.

values.name: ArrowHead.BAR_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A vertical bar bisected by the stroke, which meets the stroke at a right angle and is the same weight as the stroke. The bar's length is 4.5 times the stroke width.

values.name: ArrowHead.CIRCLE_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A hollow circle whose outline is the same weight as the stroke. The circle's diameter is 5 times the stroke width.

values.name: ArrowHead.CIRCLE_SOLID_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A solid circle whose diameter is 5 times the stroke width.

values.name: ArrowHead.CURVED_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A solid arrow head whose pierced end concaves toward the point and whose point describes a 45-degree angle.

values.name: ArrowHead.SIMPLE_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: An arrow head formed by two slanting lines whose intersection forms a 45-degree angle and whose stroke weight is the same as the path's stroke.

values.name: ArrowHead.SIMPLE_WIDE_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: An arrow head formed by two slanting lines whose intersection forms a 90-degree angle and whose stroke weight is the same as the path's stroke.

values.name: ArrowHead.SQUARE_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A hollow square set perpendicular to the path, whose outline is the same weight as the stroke. The length of one side of the square is 5 times the stroke width.

values.name: ArrowHead.SQUARE_SOLID_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A solid square set perpendicular to the end of the path. The length of one side of the square is 5 times the stroke width.

values.name: ArrowHead.TRIANGLE_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A solid triangle arrow head whose point describes a 45-degree angle.

values.name: ArrowHead.TRIANGLE_WIDE_ARROW_HEAD
values.description: A solid triangle arrow head whose point describes a 90-degree angle.

values.name: ArrowHeadAlignmentEnum.INSIDE_PATH
values.description: The arrowhead is inside the path, path geometry changes to accomodate arrow heads.

values.name: ArrowHeadAlignmentEnum.OUTSIDE_PATH
values.description: The arrowhead is outside the path i.e. path geometry remains same.

values.description: Creates a color with the luminance of the base color and the hue and saturation of the blend color. Note: Preserves gray levels and is useful for coloring monochrome images or tinting color images. Creates the inverse effect of the luminosity blend mode.

values.name: BlendMode.COLOR_BURN
values.description: Darkens the base color to reflect the blend color. Note: Blending with white produces no change.

values.name: BlendMode.COLOR_DODGE
values.description: Brightens the base color to reflect the blend color. Note: Blending with pure black produces no change.

values.name: BlendMode.DARKEN
values.description: Selects the darker of the base or blend colors as the resulting color; replaces areas lighter than the blend color but does not change areas darker than the blend color.

values.name: BlendMode.DIFFERENCE
values.description: Subtracts either the blend color from the base color or vice versa, depending on which has the greater brightness value. Note: Blending with white inverts the base color values; blending with black produces no change.

values.name: BlendMode.EXCLUSION
values.description: Creates an effect similar to--but lower in contrast than--the difference blend mode. Note: Blending with white inverts the base color values; blending with black produces no change

values.name: BlendMode.HARD_LIGHT
values.description: For blend colors lighter than 50% gray, lightens the artwork as if it were screened; for blend colors darker than 50% gray, darkens the artwork as if it were multiplied. Note: Painting with pure black or white results in pure black or white.

values.name: BlendMode.HUE
values.description: Creates a color with the luminance and saturation of the base color and the hue of the blend color.

values.name: BlendMode.LIGHTEN
values.description: Selects the lighter of the base or blend colors as the resulting color; replaces areas darker than the blend color but does not change areas lighter than the blend color

values.name: BlendMode.LUMINOSITY
values.description: Creates a color with the hue and saturation of the base color and the luminance of the blend color. Note: Creates the inverse effect of the color blend mode.

values.name: BlendMode.MULTIPLY
values.description: Multiplies the base color by the blend color, resulting in a darker color. Note: Multiplying with black produces black; multiplying with white leaves the color unchanged.

values.name: BlendMode.NORMAL
values.description: Colors the object with the blend color, without interaction with the base color.

values.name: BlendMode.OVERLAY
values.description: Multiplies or screens the colors, depending on the base color; patterns or colors overlay the existing artwork, preserving base color highlights and shadows while mixing in the blend color to reflect the lightness or darkness of the original color.

values.name: BlendMode.SATURATION
values.description: Creates a color with the luminance and hue of the base color and the saturation of the blend color. Note: Does not change areas with no saturation (0% gray).

values.name: BlendMode.SCREEN
values.description: Multiplies the inverse of the blend and base colors, resulting in a lighter color. Note: Screening with white produces white; screening with black leaves the color unchanged.

values.name: BlendMode.SOFT_LIGHT
values.description: For blend colors lighter than 50% gray, lightens the artwork as if it were dodged; for blend colors darker than 50% gray, darkens the artwork as if it were burned. Note: Painting with pure black or white produces a distinctly darker or lighter area, but does not result in pure black or white.

NestedStyleDelimiters.description: Delimiter options for marking the end of the application of the nested style.

values.description: Uses the first word or words in the paragraph as the nested style delimiter. The first word is considered all characters preceding the first space or white space character in the paragraph.

values.name: NestedStyleDelimiters.EM_SPACE

values.name: NestedStyleDelimiters.EN_SPACE
values.description: Uses the first en space as the nested style delimiter.

values.name: NestedStyleDelimiters.FORCED_LINE_BREAK

values.name: NestedStyleDelimiters.INLINE_GRAPHIC
values.description: Uses the first inline graphic as the nested style delimiter.

values.name: TrapEndTypes.OVERLAP_TRAP_ENDS
